chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from the one who narrated it to him, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar; and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from his father, from some of his companions, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The nearest that the servants are to Allah, majestic is His remembrance, and the most pleasing state of theirs to Him, is when they have lost sight of the Proof of Allah, mighty and majestic, and he has not appeared to them, and they do not know his place, while in that state they know that the Proof of Allah, majestic is His remembrance, and His covenant have not been nullified. So at that time, expect relief morning and evening.

For the most intense that the wrath of Allah is upon His enemies is when they have lost His Proof and he has not appeared to them, while He knows that His friends do not fall into doubt. Had He known that they would fall into doubt, He would not have concealed His Proof from them for the blink of an eye. And that only occurs over the heads of the worst of people.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءَهُ: His devoted friends and loyal followers
key_terms.الْفَرَجَ: relief or deliverance, especially the awaited divine opening
key_terms.حُجَّةَ اللَّهِ: Allah’s divinely appointed proof and authority over creation
key_terms.شِرَارِ النَّاسِ: the worst or most evil of people
key_terms.غَضَبُ اللَّهِ: the wrath of Allah upon His enemies
key_terms.غَيَّبَ: He caused to be concealed or hidden
key_terms.مِيثَاقُهُ: His covenant, meaning the enduring divine pledge and binding authority
key_terms.يَرْتَابُونَ: they fall into doubt or uncertainty

ai.seo_question: How should believers understand the ghaybah of Allah’s Hujjah and what attitude should they maintain during it?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that during the ghaybah (occultation) of Allah’s Hujjah, the faithful remain closest to Allah by maintaining certainty that His proof and covenant still endure. It emphasizes steadfastness without doubt, expectation of faraj, and portrays the concealment of the Hujjah as a trial that distinguishes Allah’s awliya' from His enemies.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from the one who narrated it, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from his father, from one of his companions, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The closest of what the servants can be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention, and the Happiest what He<sup>azwj</sup> can be from them is when they would be missing the Divine Authority of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Majestic and Mighty and he<sup>asws</sup> would not be apparent to them and they would not be knowing his<sup>asws</sup> place, and they, during that, would be knowing that it neither invalidates the Divine Authority of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Mention, nor His<sup>azwj</sup> Covenant. Thus, during that, they would be anticipating the relief morning and evening.

So the most intensely Wrathful what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> can be upon His<sup>azwj</sup> enemies is when they are missing His<sup>azwj</sup> Divine Authority and he<sup>asws</sup> is not apparent to them, and He<sup>azwj</sup> has Known that His<sup>azwj</sup> friends would not be suspicious, and had He<sup>azwj</sup> Known that they would be suspicious, He<sup>azwj</sup> would not have Caused His<sup>azwj</sup> Divine Authority to be absent from them for the blink of an eye, and that (Wrath) does not happen to be except upon the heads of the most evil of the people’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn Khalid from the person who narrated to him from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from ‘Abdallah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from his father from certain people of his friends from al-Mufaddal ibn ‘Umar from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“People are nearer to Allah, Majestic is Whose mention, and He is more pleased with them when the leader who possesses authority from Allah, Majestic is Whose mention, will be out of their sight. He would not publicly appear among them and they would not know his place. Despite this they would know that the leader who possesses authority from Allah, Majestic is Whose mention, is not invalidated nor is His covenant as suCh In such a case, they expect relief and happiness through his reappearance in public mornings and evenings.

Allah’s anger on His enemies is most intense when the leadership with Allah’s authority would be out of public sight and would not appear to them. He (Allah) knows that his friends do not have doubts. Had it been in His knowledge that they would doubt He would not have caused the leader with His authority to disappear from public sight not even for a blinking of an eye. The reappearance of the Leader with Divine Authority will only take place over the heads of the evil ones among the people.”
